newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply higher after stock data.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply higher after stock data.

text.p: An 8,100-tonne drop in LME stocks Friday cast aside any lingering belief in huge, off-exchange red metal hoards and triggered a rally to push COMEX over a dollar per pound by close.
"Going out the week above the dollar level probably has some psychological significance," said Smith Barney's David Rinehimer.
December COMEX settled 5.60 cents firmer at 101.45 cents per pound, traded 102.40 to 99.40 cents, the highest close for December since late June.
LME three months closed near a two and a half month high.
Volume on COMEX was heavy, estimated at 20,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 9,586 lots.
Brokers said much of the activity involved funds liquidating their short positions, with price movements accelerated by delta hedging of options.
LME stocks now total 101,175 tonnes, their lowest for six and a quarter years and well under a month's global supply.

Friday's surge was in sharp contrast to Thursday's two-cent loss when the market was unnerved by a World Bureau of Metal Statistics report suggesting that nearly 600,000 tonnes of copper were stored off-exchange in Rotterdam.
Rinehimer said sentiment was shifting to the view that stock drawdowns from LME were for consumption rather than a ploy to shift metal off-exchange.
But the higher prices and strong backwardation will be a test of how good demand really is by seeing how much, if any surplus metal goes into LME depots, Rinehimer said.
"I see no reason to chase the market here," he added. Down the road, fundamentals still pointed to copper surpluses.
COMEX stocks rose 1,019 short tons Friday to 33,769 short tons. Much of the increase was in Baltimore, up 795 short tons to 1,941 tons.

The first batch entered Baltimore on Tuesday, followed by another load Wednesday. Traders said there was talk of several thousand tons of metal, shipped from LME depots in Europe, due to be off-loaded into the East Coast location, the result of cross-exchange arbitrage deals whose economics some traders questioned.

Traders also noted a shift in the arbitrage levels. November LME closed Friday at a premium to spot COMEX, 102.42 cents to 101.25 cents. Spot COMEX had been at a premium. COMEX's December premium over December LME was down to just over 1.5 cents.
